predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the south-western Britons: Cornwall, Devon and west Somerset

successors.name: Kingdom of Cornwall
successors.text: the rump kingdom in what is today Cornwall

successors.name: Kingdom of Wessex
successors.text: Wessex's 710 shape, 9,588 km2 larger than its 705-709 shape: Devon and the rest of the Dumnonian shape outside Cornwall

ledger.x: c. 658: Cenwalh of Wessex takes eastern and central Somerset. 'in 658 his army met the Britons for a climactic battle at Peonnum' (the infobox says 'about AD 660'); he 'advanced west through the Polden Hills to the River Parrett, annexing eastern and central Somerset', 'modest in size'; the Dumnonia page: 'the eastern…
By 685: Wessex reaches the Bristol Channel.
710: the kingdom of Dumnonia gives way to a Cornish rump.

wars.name: Battle of Peonnum
wars.outcome: Cenwalh's West Saxons beat the Britons and annexed eastern and central Somerset as far as the Parrett, which stayed the border until 681-685.

wars.name: West Saxon advance to the Bristol Channel
wars.outcome: Centwine of Wessex wins and the West Saxons occupy 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel'.

wars.name: Ine of Wessex against Geraint
wars.outcome: 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex.'

certainty.note: Only the Parrett frontier of 658-685 is named on the pages; the rest is approximate.
